stories.title: Monza memories - Italian GP in pictures through the years
stories.summary: The Italian Grand Prix takes place this weekend at Monza, arguably the most historic venue on the calendar. Monza has hosted Formula 1 races more times than any other circuit, staging grands prix in all but one year since the inaugural season in 1950. The only time Monza was absent was 1980, when it was being renovated. Located in a royal park and surrounded by woodland, it is known as the 'cathedral of speed'. It is the spiritual home of Ferrari and the devoted tifosi who adore the Italian team. It is all but impossible to imagine F1 without Monza - it was where the first world championship was decided 76 years ago and where, last year, Red Bull's Max Verstappen set the fastest lap in F1 history during qualifying. Throughout the years, Monza has been the scene of thrilling finishes, Ferrari glory, title wins, controversy and tragedy. Its story is F1's story. Here is a selection of images through the years... A picture from the 1950 Italian Grand Prix, the final race of Formula 1's first season. The race and inaugural drivers' title was won by Italian Giuseppe Farina, in an Alfa Romeo. Farina is the only driver to win the title in his home country.

stories.title: Surge in orders for repellent made with Aomori chilli pepper amid more bear sightings
stories.summary: A bear repellent called "Kuma wo Boru", made with bhut jolokia chilli and pyroligneous acid, is gaining popularity amid increased bear sightings in Japan. The repellent uses natural ingredients and comes in two forms: a hanging bottle and a portable solid, releasing capsaicin to keep bears away. Orders have surged nationwide, especially from individuals in urban areas, as bears increasingly enter cities, highlighting efforts to promote human-bear coexistence. Amid a series of bear sightings across Japan, a bear repellent made with bhut jolokia – a super-hot chilli pepper cultivated in Aomori prefecture – is gaining attention. In addition to its exceptional effectiveness at keeping bears away, the product is characterised by its use of naturally derived ingredients, which contribute to environmental protection. For these reasons, an online shop is receiving orders from all over the country. Named “Kuma wo Boru”, which means “to chase away bears” in the local dialect, this product is manufactured by Eco Work, a company based in Goshogawara in Aomori in northern Honshu. It is formulated with pyroligneous acid – a by-product of charcoal burning – and ingredients such as bhut jolokia, or “ghost pepper”. When used, the pungent compound capsaicin is released into the air. The product comes in two forms: a plastic bottle for hanging with a slit at the top, designed to release the scent from the liquid inside, and a solid form that can be carried in a pouch. According to Iki Sangyo, a company based in Sendai, Miyagi prefecture that operates an online store, orders began to increase about two years ago. In 2025, orders from businesses reached a record high.

stories.title: Singapore may require social media firms to set daily time limits for teens
stories.summary: Singapore plans to introduce legislation early next year requiring social media platforms to roll out stronger safeguards for teens, including possibly setting a daily time limit, Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo has said. If a platform could not or did not want to introduce these stronger safeguards, Singapore intended to raise the minimum age of access to that platform to 18, Teo told journalists in an interview on Friday.
